name: com.scorecompute/scorecompute
title: ScoreCompute
description: 40 MCP tools: Rust computation, Discovery, composition, counterexample scans and signed checks.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Verify a structured arithmetic, cash-flow (XNPV/XIRR), A/B test, statistics, shadow, ephemeris or route claim with a bounded native engine. Returns a model-scoped verdict and portable Ed25519 server receipt; never truth, authenticity, financial advice or fraud certification. Route claims explicitly distinguish optimality from a supplied tour total. Native failures return no scientific verdict. Parameters and examples: /verify and /docs/mcp/.

tools.name: check_arithmetic
tools.description: Check an explicit arithmetic claim. Checked i128 rationals give exact verdicts when expression, claim and tolerances are representable. Unsupported functions or overflow return an estimate with an undetermined verdict. Includes a versioned integrity digest; no checks of units or model meaning.

tools.name: audit_statistics
tools.description: Apply necessary GRIM/GRIMMER checks to rounded means and sample deviations of bounded integer observations. Passing does not prove a dataset exists; inconsistency does not establish fraud.

tools.name: propagate_uncertainty
tools.description: Check dimensions, then compare first-order GUM with seeded fixed-sample Monte Carlo for an explicit model of 1–16 inputs. Return uncertainty budgets, coverage intervals and convergence/linearization findings. Conditional on supplied distributions; no affine units. CPU, direct-only; no planner binding.

correlations.description: Correlations between normal inputs with standard_uncertainty > 0.

expression.description: Model with + - * / ^, parentheses, pi and sqrt exp ln log10 sin cos tan asin acos atan abs. Literals are dimensionless; no implicit multiplication.

result_unit.description: Output unit; must match the model dimension.

samples.description: Monte Carlo draws, default 1000000 (JCGM 101 typical value for 2 significant digits).

half_width.description: uniform and triangular only: half-width, in unit.

standard_uncertainty.description: normal only: standard deviation, in unit.

unit.description: e.g. mg, km/h, kg/m^3, W/m^2/K, deg, kWh, %. Empty means dimensionless. °C and °F are refused; use K.

tools.name: evaluate_ab_test
tools.description: Fixed-horizon statistics for a two-group conversion A/B test from counts: rates, absolute and relative difference (variant minus control), two-sided pooled two-proportion z-test p-value, Newcombe hybrid score (Wilson) confidence interval for the difference, and the sample size per group for a stated baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, alpha and power. Assumes independent groups evaluated once; no correction for peeking, sequential or multiple testing; no exact test; not a business recommendation.

confidence_level.description: Confidence level of the interval for the difference; default 0.95.

conversions.description: Visitors who converted; at most visitors.
Visitors who converted; at most visitors.

baseline_rate.description: Assumed true conversion rate of the control group.

minimum_detectable_effect.description: Signed effect to detect: target rate minus baseline when effect_type is absolute, that difference divided by the baseline when relative (0.1 means +10 %). The absolute effect must be at least 0.000001 in magnitude and the target rate strictly between 0 and 1.

tools.name: compute_cashflow_metrics
tools.description: Net present value and internal rate of return of 2-360 dated cash flows. NPV at a stated annual effective rate, Actual/365 Fixed day count as in spreadsheet XNPV. XIRR-style rate by a bracketed, bounded search that says when no rate exists, when several may exist or when it did not converge. Arithmetic only: no currency conversion, tax rule or financial advice.

discount_rate.description: Annual effective rate as a fraction (0.08 for 8 %). Omit to skip the NPV.

amount.description: Signed amount in one currency: negative paid out, positive received.

tools.name: scan_counterexample
tools.description: Bounded deterministic float64 scan of a scalar <= or >= claim over a declared grid of 1–6 variables. Reports numerical witnesses, undefined and uncertain evaluations, and the exact stop reason. A propagated screening guard rejects near-boundary candidates; it is not a certified interval or formal proof. An inconclusive outcome preserves unresolved sampled cells; absence of a witness does not establish the claim over the continuous box.

tools.name: verify_shadows
tools.description: Check measured shadows using NOAA solar position, a ground-plane homography from 4–16 controls and Monte Carlo uncertainty. Returns conditional consistency, never image authenticity.

tools.name: check_shadow_track
tools.description: Compare 4–120 measured minute/azimuth pairs with solar motion: residuals, slope, direction and time-lapse speed. Supply measurements, not video. Results are model-conditional consistency findings.

tools.name: check_ephemeris
tools.description: Check a claimed Sun (sun/soleil) or Moon (moon/lune) position for UTC time/location using NOAA/Meeus approximations and lunar parallax. Returns model-conditional angular consistency and lunar phase.

tools.name: plan_golden_hour
tools.description: Compute UTC start and end times of golden hour (solar elevation -4° to +6°), blue hour (-6° to -4°) and conventional sunrise and sunset (-0.833°) for one UTC day at a latitude and longitude, 1900–2100. Purely geometric: no refraction, terrain or weather. Numerical tolerance is not astronomical accuracy.

date_utc.description: Real Gregorian UTC midnight, year 1900–2100. Rust also validates month/day and leap years. Other hours are rejected, never truncated; this is not a local civil day.

tools.name: route_optimizer
tools.description: Order 2–256 points from index 0 using planar or spherical kilometre distances. Exact only after completed Held–Karp search (at most 13 points); otherwise bounded heuristics. Returns every leg and stop reason. No roads or traffic.

tools.name: optimize_tasks
tools.description: Exactly maximize value for up to 32 independent, indivisible tasks within an integer-minute budget. Each task is selected at most once; no prerequisites or shared resources.

tools.name: simulate_plan
tools.description: Estimate deadline success, mean duration and empirical p95 for up to 32 integer-minute tasks under independent bounded uniform duration variations. Seeded CPU sampling; not a real-world forecast guarantee.

tools.name: build_robust_plan
tools.description: Compare up to three task selections; choose highest examined value meeting the target under simultaneous 95% sampling bounds or an exact bound. Independent-uniform durations; can return inconclusive/blocked. Streams native events.

tools.name: improve_schedule
tools.description: Compare up to 32 declared deadline/optional-task changes under independent-uniform durations; preserve required tasks. Search bounds select one finalist for separately seeded confirmation, without retries. Conditional on the model, not delivery reliability.

extra_minutes.description: Unique permitted deadline increments; include zero and keep every modified deadline at most 1440 minutes.

removal_sets.description: Unique sorted sets of optional original task indices; include the empty set, preserve required tasks, and keep at least one task.

tools.name: analyze_kinematics
tools.description: Convert angular speed and candidate distances to minimum transverse speeds; check a claimed speed-distance pair. Distance hypotheses are supplied, not measured; no object-origin conclusion.

tools.name: triangulate_tracks
tools.description: Fit position/velocity from 2–4 supplied azimuth/elevation tracks using constant velocity in spherical ECEF and declared angular noise/clocks. Reports fit status and conditional local uncertainty; no object identification or calibrated accuracy.

clock_offset_s.description: The observer clock is ahead of the common base by this many seconds; the engine subtracts it.

t_s.description: Seconds from a common epoch, strictly increasing for this observer.

tools.name: simulate_pi
tools.description: Estimate pi with seeded Monte Carlo and a 95% Wilson interval; up to 5 million samples. CPU or optional CUDA. Other direct scientific engines run on CPU.

tools.name: solve_equilibrium
tools.description: Solve Kuhn poker with CFR+ self-play, measure exploitability with pure best responses and compare the game value with -1/18. Illustrative game theory, not gambling advice.

tools.name: analyze_chess_game
tools.description: Compare 4–40 supplied FEN positions and played SAN/UCI moves with Stockfish: first-choice agreement and centipawn loss. Entire analysis has a 25-second deadline; no cheating verdict.

tools.name: screen_wash_trading
tools.description: Screen a supplied trade series for repeated volume at nearly equal prices within a declared time window. Return recycled-volume ratio and cycles; a pattern does not prove wash trading.

tools.name: forge_route_policy
tools.description: Search for a custom scoring formula that builds closed 2D tours, trained on 1–8 supplied point sets (at most 64 attempts and 31 nodes; stops between trials after 25 s). Returns an inspectable formula runnable with run_route_policy. Experimental: scored on the supplied training cases only, with no held-out validation, arbitrary code or automatic promotion.

tools.name: run_route_policy
tools.description: Execute a supplied bounded score AST on 2–128 Euclidean-km points with depot 0 and 2-opt. Validates the closed tour; exact=false. No retraining, external effects or promotion. Hashes identify programs, not independent validation.

tools.name: plan_observation
tools.description: Given azimuth/elevation tracks of one moving object, rank 1–64 proposed future observation series by predicted position uncertainty and declared cost. Assumes constant velocity, independent new errors and exact stations and clocks. Supply future times and noise, never candidate angles or a baseline. A forecast, not a measurement or visibility proof.

clock_offset_s.description: The observer clock is ahead of the common base by this many seconds; the engine subtracts it.

t_s.description: Seconds from a common epoch, strictly increasing for this observer.

observations.description: Original angular observations; Rust computes the baseline fit and covariance itself.

sample_times_s.description: Proposed corrected times, strictly increasing, after the last original observation and no later than the common horizon. No measured or simulated angles are accepted here.

horizon_s.description: Absolute comparison time in the same corrected seconds as the observations; after the original observations, within their bounded 3600-second domain.

tools.name: assimilate_observation
tools.description: Refit original tracks plus one supplied new angular series, each counted once; compute the baseline natively. Declare synthetic/measured origin (unverified). Conditional uncertainty may worsen; forecast angles are not acquired evidence.

clock_offset_s.description: The observer clock is ahead of the common base by this many seconds; the engine subtracts it.

t_s.description: Seconds from a common epoch, strictly increasing for this observer.
Already corrected absolute time; strictly after all baseline samples and no later than the comparison horizon.

horizon_s.description: Absolute comparison time in the same corrected seconds as the observations; after the original observations, within their bounded 3600-second domain.

data_origin.description: Origin declared by the caller; even measured is not independently verified or authenticated.

tools.name: stress_test_observation
tools.description: Refit 1–32 declared hypothetical angular/clock perturbations to challenge reconstruction stability. Explicit hypothetical acknowledgement required. Non-convergence is inconclusive; none_found covers examined cases only. No new observations.

clock_offset_s.description: The observer clock is ahead of the common base by this many seconds; the engine subtracts it.

t_s.description: Seconds from a common epoch, strictly increasing for this observer.

evaluation_time_s.description: Absolute corrected time, within 3600 seconds of the first corrected original measurement.

clock_offset_delta_s.description: Hypothetical change to the declared clock correction, not to the measured timestamps.

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description: Read native contracts, themes, units, assumptions, backends and approved composition families; optional exact theme filter. tools/list discovers direct MCP tools; list_composition_capabilities adds planner bindings.

tools.name: plan_mission
tools.description: Preview robust scheduling without running engines: validate assumptions/permissions and return up to three candidate budgets (nominal, 10% reserve, 20% reserve), compute limits or blockers. No arbitrary tools or external code.

tools.name: list_composition_capabilities
tools.description: Read implemented versioned contracts, native capabilities, approved adapters and planning examples. Unsupported unit/model facts expose missing adapters. No engines run; direct tools remain independently callable.

tools.name: compose_capabilities
tools.description: Find a multi-tool workflow from declared available inputs to a goal output, for example task selection or routing followed by deadline-risk simulation. Returns the steps, blockers and existing-tool bindings within tool, locality and search bounds. Cost counts graph steps, not speed, price or quality. Runs no engines; execution validates arguments.

tools.name: execute_composition
tools.description: Run approved task-selection/route-to-duration risk chains only. Supply engine inputs and explicit uncertainty; route speed is 1–150 km/h. Returns native receipts and 95% sampling bounds. Completed means assessed, not safe. Other paths use advertised bindings.

tools.name: network_status
tools.description: Read contributor availability, offered CPU/GPU resources and verified throughput by workload. Hardware is self-reported; per-GPU VRAM is not pooled. Mixed-workload samples do not measure comparative speed.

tools.name: submit_network_job
tools.description: Queue fixed public synthetic pi (CPU/CUDA) or one of three discrete schedule scenarios (CPU only). No private data/custom code. Returns a ticket; poll get_network_job. Coordinator recomputes every accepted shard; no net speedup claim. Jobs may expire.

tools.name: get_network_job
tools.description: Read a public contributor ticket/progress and verified pi or discrete synthetic schedule result. Schedule results include fixed-sample Wilson95 bounds. Worker/verification/wall times are separate; model probabilities are not delivery guarantees.

tools.name: compute_orbit
tools.description: Compute an ideal two-body Keplerian orbit around one solar mass. Time starts at periapsis; distances use AU and time uses days. This model is not a real celestial ephemeris.

tools.name: hear_the_shape
tools.description: Compute 1–12 ideal fixed/free membrane modes for a simple polygon in metres using bounded P1 finite elements. Return upper bounds, extrapolated estimates and optional frequencies/shapes. Finite spectral agreement does not prove isospectrality; no damping. CPU, direct-only; no planner binding.

boundary.description: fixed (default): drumhead, TM waveguide. free: acoustic cavity, TE waveguide.

compare_polygon.description: Optional second shape: do the two drums sound the same?

include_mode_shapes.description: Adds a ≤1024-triangle mesh with normalized mode values, for visualization.

polygon.description: Vertices [x, y] in metres, either orientation; a repeated closing vertex is allowed. Must be simple.

wave_speed.description: m/s; √(tension/areal density) for a membrane. Enables frequency_hz and notes.

tools.name: kepler_stability
tools.description: Survey up to 512 initial orbits in a planar circular Sun–Jupiter model; at most 4 million reserved CPU steps. Return finite-window sensitivity, actual durations, sampled Jacobi drift and explicit stops. Bands do not prove chaos or stability; radial overlap is not an encounter. Direct-only.

tools.name: shape_the_sound
tools.description: Kac's question in reverse: design a polygonal drumhead whose lowest tones play requested frequency ratios (a fifth, a triad, a pentatonic scale), each accepted within ±tolerance_cents. proven_impossible is returned only when proven theorems exclude every ratio combination inside those tolerance windows for a connected uniform membrane with a fixed edge: simple fundamental, f2/f1 ≤ j11/j01 ≈ 1.5933 with equality for the disk (Ashbaugh–Benguria 1992), and Yang's universal inequality minimized exactly over the window box; an exact-target exclusion is reported separately. Otherwise multi-start L-BFGS with exact finite-element shape derivatives designs a 5–16-vertex polygon, then reanalyses it on three refined meshes with the shared hear_the_shape solver: achieved ratios, errors in cents with estimated uncertainty (not rigorous bounds), resolution warnings, optional numerical tuning of the fundamental in Hz. not_achieved is a bounded-search result, never an impossibility proof. Ideal membrane only.

fundamental_hz.description: With wave_speed: scale the drum so its fundamental sounds at this frequency.

include_mode_shapes.description: Adds computed mode shapes from the shared forward solver (≤1024 triangles, full-precision coordinates) for visualization.

max_evaluations.description: Search budget in finite-element evaluations, default 300.

target_ratios.description: Frequency ratios f2/f1, f3/f1, … of the lowest modes, ascending (e.g. [1.25, 1.5] for a just major triad).

tolerance_cents.description: Success when |error| + uncertainty ≤ tolerance for every ratio; default 5 cents.

tools.name: tour_profile
tools.description: Describe the layout of 3–256 planar points: pairwise distances, nearest-neighbour isolation, centroid spread, PCA collinearity, principal-axis mirror symmetry and a distance histogram, all scale-normalized. Useful to characterize or compare point sets before routing. Rounded fingerprints are descriptive, not proofs of equivalence or method benefit.
